name: Jack's Camp
positioning: Vintage-style tented safari camp in Botswana's Makgadikgadi Salt Pans, set in a one million-acre private wildlife reserve
best_for: Travelers wanting a desert safari with meerkat encounters and quad biking on the salt pans
Guests who love tents filled with Persian rugs, antique furniture and natural history collections

facts.text: Jack's Camp is in Botswana's Makgadikgadi Salt Pans, the remnants of an enormous super-lake that once covered most of Southern Africa.
Adventurer Jack Bousfield set up the first camp on the site in the 1960s.
Tent interiors feature rich textiles from around the world, cabinets of curiosities, Persian rugs and hand-carved beds.
Framed Peter Beard pictures hang alongside original posters from French taxidermist Deyrolle and Bousfield family photos.
Tents have an over-bed cooling system and an en-suite bathroom with indoor and outdoor showers.
Afternoon tea with cucumber sandwiches and biscuits is served in a round tent strewn with Persian rugs and giant cushions.
Spa treatments are available at additional cost.
A helicopter flight over the Makgadikgadi Pans can be taken with doors on or off.
Guests can explore the desert landscape on horseback.
Between March and April the pans are a flamingo breeding site.
Wildlife includes aardwolves, bat-eared foxes, honey badgers and black-maned Kalahari lion.

highlights.text: Each guest tent has an expansive deck with a private plunge pool and views of the Makgadikgadi Salt Pans.
The camp has pioneered a meerkat habituation project with researchers, and guests can meet the habituated meerkats.
Jack's Camp is one of three camps in a one million-acre private wildlife reserve.
From November to March, 30,000 zebra and wildebeest arrive on the pans in Africa's second largest migration.
Guided quad biking crosses the salt-crusted pans.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes the remote desert location requires charter flight access.
